clue.text: Morse finally departed, keeps missing Lewis really

indicators.note: something departed has left, so the picked letter leaves the phrase

parts.note: someone who keeps missing a blow dodges on, continuing to evade it

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word Morse

explanation.surface: With Inspector Morse dead, his sidekick Lewis keeps failing to catch the villain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes E from Morse, and 'departed' removes that E from DODGES ON. Morse and Lewis look like the TV detectives, but Lewis is Lewis Carroll.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis Carroll was the pen name of the Oxford mathematician Charles Dodgson, so his real surname answers 'Lewis really'.

clue.text: Bibulous youth gains a little weight

indicators.note: the word for youth gains something inside it, taking it in

parts.note: a youth is a boy
oz is the abbreviation for ounce, a small weight

explanation.surface: A hard-drinking young man is putting on a few pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Bibulous means fond of drink, the same as a drunken, alcohol-soaked character.

clue.text: See what's finally right for you, and partner too

indicators.note: finally signals taking the closing letter of each of the following five words

explanation.surface: Look at what is ultimately correct for you and for your partner as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what's finally' tells you to take the last letters of right, for, you, partner and too. See is a noun here: a bishop's seat.
explanation.definitionFit: A see is a bishop's diocese, and this Cornish city has a cathedral and is the seat of a bishop.

clue.text: Home lover to do bathroom up for the kids

parts.note: in means at home
a fan is a lover of something
to tile is to cover a bathroom's walls, doing it up

explanation.surface: A house-proud DIY enthusiast renovates the bathroom for the children.
explanation.definitionFit: Childish or suitable for small children is the sense of this adjective, so 'for the kids' fits.

clue.text: Abroad, mere lass I sheltered from blows

parts.note: a gal is a lass
the lee side is the side sheltered from the wind

explanation.surface: A girl abroad says she was protected from being beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: Mere is the old word for a lake, so 'Abroad, mere' is a foreign lake; blows are gusts of wind, not punches.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sea of Galilee in Israel is actually a freshwater lake, a mere in a foreign land.

clue.text: Did long period of time set back study?

parts.note: a year is a period of time

indicators.note: set back means the word for study is placed in reverse order

parts.note: a den is a private study room

explanation.surface: Did a long spell of time put back my study plans?
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to yearn, so 'did long' is the past tense of that verb.

clue.text: A "best friend"'s tragic error defending nursing practice

indicators.note: nursing means holding something inside, as the word for tragic holds another

parts.note: sad means tragic
usage means customary practice
OG is an own goal, a defender's error in football

explanation.surface: A dog's tragic mistake guarding a nursing practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nursing' sets the practice word inside the tragic one, splitting it after two letters. A dog is man's best friend, hence the quotation marks; OG, an own goal, is a defender's error in football.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog is proverbially man's best friend, and the dachshund is nicknamed for its long sausage shape.

clue.text: I don't believe that a riddle should be shortened

indicators.note: shortened means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to riddle is to sift through a coarse sieve

explanation.surface: Someone sceptically insists a riddle ought to be made shorter.
explanation.walkthrough: A riddle is a coarse sieve, so to riddle is to sift; 'should be shortened' cuts the final T.
explanation.definitionFit: This exclamation expresses scornful disbelief, exactly what 'I don't believe that' says.

clue.text: Reading for one's teacher at first and for oneself?

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of the word teacher

parts.note: own means belonging to oneself

explanation.surface: Is reading for the teacher at first and then for one's own pleasure?
explanation.walkthrough: Reading is the English town in Berkshire, not the activity; the capital R is hidden at the start of the sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Reading is a large town in Berkshire, so it is an example of an urban settlement.

clue.text: Old fogies excited by South London location

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Elderly fuddy-duddies get worked up about part of South London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South London' looks like the definition, but South gives only S; the area is in East London's docklands.
explanation.definitionFit: This peninsula in a bend of the Thames in East London is home to Canary Wharf, a London district.

clue.text: Local pain that's total restricting Bob moving around

indicators.note: restricting means holding in, so the word for total encloses another piece

parts.note: pure means total, as in pure nonsense

indicators.note: moving around means the letters of Bob are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tedious drinker at the local pub totally hems in Bob as he moves about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving around' reorders Bob's letters before 'restricting' puts them inside the word for total. A local is a British neighbourhood pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A local is a neighbourhood pub, and a pain is a tiresome person, so a boring drinker there fits.

clue.text: After working, we're on day's leave again

indicators.note: after working means once the letters have been worked over into a new order

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: After work, we're off for the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After working' rearranges WE'RE ON plus D, the abbreviation for day. Leave is the verb to bequeath, not a holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow is to bequeath money to an institution, so to leave it funds again is a second endowment.

clue.text: Triumph in Sun competition?

parts.note: winning a contest held on Sunday, or a newspaper prize, is read as prevailing on the day

explanation.surface: Someone wins a newspaper's prize contest.
explanation.walkthrough: Sun suggests the tabloid newspaper, but it is the abbreviation for Sunday: a victory in that day's contest.
explanation.definitionFit: To prevail or be victorious in a contest is the idiomatic meaning of this phrase.

clue.text: Taking one's time, no longer rush forward at first

parts.note: hie is an archaic word for hurry, no longer in use

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of the word forward

explanation.surface: Taking your time is no longer the thing; rush forward first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no longer' marks HIE as archaic. The definition reads 'taking one', one who takes things.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who takes what is not theirs is a robber, so 'taking one' describes a stealer.

clue.text: A grass briefly run in turning over scandalous info

indicators.note: in means the shortened word goes inside the reversed one
turning over means the word for scandalous info is read backwards

parts.note: mud is scandalous information, as in mudslinging

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: An informer, run in briefly, turns over the dirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning over' reads the scandal word backwards and 'in' puts the clipped run inside it. Grass suggests a police informer, but here it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Durum is a hard wheat used for pasta, and wheat is a cereal grass.

clue.text: Note starter of lobster, chopped and chilled

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: starter of takes the opening letter of the word lobster

parts.note: axed means chopped

explanation.surface: A recipe note: start with lobster, chopped and chilled.
explanation.walkthrough: Chilled suggests food from a fridge, but it is slang for calm and at ease.
explanation.definitionFit: Chilled is informal for calm and at ease, which is what an untroubled person is.

clue.text: What starts with cook, posh, joining French navy?

parts.note: to do food is to cook it
U means upper-class, posh
bleu is French for blue, navy being dark blue

explanation.surface: A dish that starts with posh cooking and joins French navy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What starts with' is a riddling definition: the word with begins with the letter W.
explanation.definitionFit: The word with begins with the letter W, and this is how that letter's name is spelt out.

clue.text: Furniture style suitable for autumn?

parts.note: a table with hinged flaps is read as a season when foliage falls

explanation.walkthrough: Autumn is when leaves drop from trees; the table has a hinged flap, also called a leaf, that drops down.
explanation.definitionFit: A table with hinged flaps that fold down is a common style of furniture.

clue.text: Drug employed in solution for stiffening collar

indicators.note: employed in means put inside the word for stiffening solution

parts.note: size is a gluey solution used to stiffen paper or cloth
E is ecstasy, the drug

explanation.surface: A drug is used in the starch for stiffening a shirt collar.
explanation.walkthrough: Collar looks like part of the shirt, but it is the verb to grab or arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: To collar someone is to grab or arrest them, the same as to take hold of them.

clue.text: Sky forbidden to show drama: races have to be broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means put out over the air, so the words are spoken

parts.note: noh is Japanese drama, flies are races, and own means have

explanation.surface: Sky TV is banned from airing a drama because the races must be shown.
explanation.walkthrough: Sky looks like the broadcaster, but it is airspace. Noh is classical Japanese drama, and flies are races, as in a sprint.
explanation.definitionFit: This is airspace where aircraft are prohibited from flying, so a forbidden stretch of sky.

clue.text: Cry from Japanese stops viewer being heard

indicators.note: being heard means the words are spoken aloud

parts.note: to ban is to stop, and an eye is a viewer

explanation.surface: Someone shouts in Japanese to stop a spectator.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a Japanese battle cry or cheer, meaning roughly 'ten thousand years'.

clue.text: Trouble in store for tailors

indicators.note: trouble means disturb, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: There is trouble ahead for the tailors.
explanation.walkthrough: Tailors looks like the tradespeople, but it is the verb: adapts to suit.
explanation.definitionFit: To tailor something is to adapt or adjust it to a purpose, which is to direct its focus.

clue.text: Proceeds to bow

definitions.meaning: proceeds are the money produced or returned, the output from an investment
to bow down is to submit or give way

explanation.definitionFit: The noun means the amount produced, and the verb means give way or submit.

clue.text: Coach prepared to make scene?

parts.note: a stage, or stagecoach, is a horse-drawn coach
set means prepared, ready

explanation.surface: A trainer gets ready to make a fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: Coach suggests a trainer, but it is a stagecoach.
explanation.definitionFit: Scenery built for a theatre production makes up the scene the audience sees.

clue.text: Soap person uses close to face, equally soft

indicators.note: close to means the end of the word face

parts.note: as tender means just as soft

explanation.surface: A person who uses soap near the face, as it is equally gentle.
explanation.walkthrough: Soap looks like the cleanser, but it is the TV soap opera EastEnders, a BBC serial set in East London.
explanation.definitionFit: A character in the BBC soap opera EastEnders, or a resident of East London, fits 'soap person'.

clue.text: Her angling of the coarse variety?

definitions.text: Her angling of the coarse variety?

parts.words: Her angling of the coarse variety?
parts.note: a woman who fishes in coarse waters, and also a loud foul-mouthed woman

explanation.walkthrough: Coarse fishing in Britain is fishing for freshwater fish other than salmon and trout; coarse also means vulgar.
explanation.definitionFit: A coarse-mouthed, loud woman is so called after the market women who sold fish.

clue.text: From rear of boat, unwound extra net

parts.note: aft is the rear part of a ship

indicators.note: unwound means unravelled, so the letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: From the back of the boat, the spare fishing net was paid out.
explanation.walkthrough: Net looks like a fishing net, but it is the adjective: income after deductions.
explanation.definitionFit: Net income is what remains after deductions, so pay left once the taxman takes his share.

clue.text: Wine bar organised internet conference

indicators.note: organised means arranged, so the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A wine bar set up an online meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminar held over the web is an online conference.

clue.text: Occasional thing prisoners do is eccentric

parts.note: odd means occasional, as in the odd visit
bird is slang for a prison sentence, from birdlime, rhyming slang for time

explanation.surface: An occasional thing that convicts do is peculiar.
explanation.walkthrough: Bird is British slang for a prison term: prisoners 'do bird'.
explanation.definitionFit: A strange or peculiar person is often described with this idiom.

clue.text: Landed bad actor in place of the Three Wise Men

definitions.text: place of the Three Wise Men

parts.note: got means landed, as in landed a job
a ham is a bad, overacting performer

explanation.surface: A poor performer arrived at the birthplace of the Magi.
explanation.walkthrough: The Three Wise Men suggest the Nativity, but the nursery rhyme has three wise men of this village go to sea in a bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: The English nursery rhyme tells of three wise men of this village who went to sea in a bowl.

clue.text: Quietly hugely impressed, and touched

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
awed means filled with wonder, hugely impressed

explanation.surface: Quietly overwhelmed, and emotionally moved.
explanation.walkthrough: Touched suggests moved emotionally, but here it means handled clumsily with the hands.
explanation.definitionFit: To handle something clumsily with the hands or paws is to have felt it, as in pawed at.

clue.text: Two small boys meeting princess?

parts.note: Roy is a boy's name
Al is short for Albert or Alan, a small boy's name

explanation.surface: Two little lads meet a princess.
explanation.definitionFit: A princess is a member of the monarch's family, so she belongs to the regal household.
